requirements.requirement: The system must include provenance metadata fields in all EvaluateCare facade responses for each quality measure returned.

The system must preserve all provenance attributes defined in the schema (source_type, source_name, api_endpoint, dataset_id, retrieval_timestamp, version) when mapping domain objects to API responses.
The system must ensure EvaluateCare facade outputs remain backward compatible by not removing or renaming existing response fields.
The system must serialize provenance metadata correctly in JSON responses without causing schema validation errors in existing clients.
The system must ensure tool_router can process responses containing provenance metadata without runtime errors or dropped fields.
The system must include provenance metadata for both provider and clinical trial evaluation responses when available.
The system must maintain consistent provenance structure across all response types to enable downstream explanation components to consume it uniformly.
The system must not alter or overwrite provenance metadata values received from upstream services (EVAL-DATA-PROV-S2).
The system must ensure that each measure object in the response includes a non-null provenance block when upstream data provides it.
The system must gracefully handle missing provenance metadata by returning a structured empty or partial provenance object without breaking the response schema.
The system must log a warning when provenance metadata is missing for any measure in the facade layer.
The system must ensure that response serialization performance does not degrade beyond acceptable thresholds when including provenance metadata.
The system must expose provenance metadata in a format that LLM-based explanation components can parse without additional transformation.
The system must ensure provenance metadata fields are explicitly labeled and human-readable to support downstream explanation generation.
The system must ensure that provenance metadata inclusion does not introduce ambiguity or duplication in measure-level data presented to LLM consumers.
